newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: No bidders for Philippine steel firm stake.
newsitem.headline: No bidders for Philippine steel firm stake.

text.p: The Philippines' National Steel Corp (NSC) said on Wednesday it had not received any bids for a 20 percent stake in the company.
The formerly state-owned NSC was recently taken over by Malaysia's Wing Tiek Holdings Bhd which, along with its partner Marubeni Corp, owns 75 percent.
Twelve firms, including several Japanese firms, had expressed interest in bidding for a 20 percent stake the government is now selling.
But at the scheduled bidding on Wednesday not a single bid was found, Arthur Aguilar, general manager of the National Development Co which manages NSC said.
Aguilar said the 20 percent stake, equivalent to over 448 million shares, was to be bidded out in four equal blocks.
The National Development Co had set a floor price of 10 pesos per share.
Among those who had expressed interest at a pre-bidding conference were Tomen Corp, Mitsui & Co Ltd, Kawasho Corp, Marubeni Corp, Urban Bank, and APC Group Inc.
The government wants to sell the remaining 5.0 percent stake to small investors at a later date.
The NSC is one of the major steel producers in the country with 39 percent of the domestic market.
NSC officials were not immediately available to comment on the absence of bidders at Wednesday's auction.
